issues.issue: Printed Chapter XCIX is sequential editorial chapter C because an earlier printed chapter number was duplicated; preserve both labels without inventing extra source.
Animodar begins under the divider on original PDF539/printed505 and ends on original PDF540/printed506 before a separately titled Chapter C begins PDF541.
Earlier Trutine of Hermes merchant horoscope and later accident-based rectification are separate procedures and must not be conflated with Animodar.
Lilly attributes the method to Ptolemy, but this source batch does not independently authenticate the Ptolemaic passage or authorship.
The original condition is preceding NEW Moon degree, or preceding FULL Moon degree of whichever luminary was ABOVE the Earth; do not choose either luminary at will.
Syzygy date/time and solar/lunar longitudes are author asserted and not independently astronomically reconstructed.
Selecting the 'most essential dignities' at syzygy degree depends on the exact period domicile, exaltation, triplicity and term tables, not current arbitrary astrological scoring weights.
The dignity score and tie rule are separate: when two planets tie in dignity, Lilly prefers the planet closest to the Ascendant.
Comparison of the chosen planet's natal zodiacal degree to Ascendant and Midheaven presumes consistent circular/angular longitude metric and house geometry; no independent chart has been recast.
Animodar may adjust the Ascendant OR Midheaven depending on proximity, so its outputs are branching angular targets, not one universal rectification operation.
The worked merchant chart was ALREADY rectified by life accidents; matching it is retrospective concordance with a potentially fitted target, not independently known true birth time.
The initial estimated time is said to differ by no more than approximately one ascending degree from the accident-adjusted chart; no actual birth clock certificate exists.
The cited 15 September 1616 syzygy four days before September 19 birth is author reported and dependent on Julian date convention.
The full Moon is placed about 11 o'clock in the daytime with Sun at Libra 2°32 above the horizon; local geographic clock and syzygy definition are unresolved.
Saturn's claimed exaltation, triplicity and term rights at Libra 2°32 are source assertions with no independent essential-dignity reference recheck.
The natal sign glyph at nine degrees of Saturn's position requires an independent diplomatic zoom to avoid a wrong sign name; the outcome is source claimed Capricorn 9°02 Ascendant.
Venus is explicitly mentioned as a rival candidate by some practitioners, a rule-ranking ambiguity, not separate observed proof.
The source describes a 'strange concurrence' if Venus were chosen, but omits a numerical alternative result, making that branch unscorable.
Lilly explicitly says neither Animodar nor Trutine is as sure as accident-based rectification; do not relabel him an unqualified advocate.
Applying these techniques to children before observed accidents is a reported fallback method, not evidence of accurate future forecasts.
The next Chapter C declares practical failure of some transit/profection procedures; navigation-only statement belongs to its own chapter.
No independent natal birth time, controlled out-of-sample accuracy, verified rectification target, medical effect or empirical astrological prediction is established.
